name: Connla (Conla, Conlaí, Conle)

attributes.attribute: the place that draws the heroes

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The record gathers the Adventures, the tales in which a man of this world is drawn away to the Otherworld. In the Adventised she told of Connla, a fairy woman lures the youth to the Otherworld. In the tale of Cormac, that king is drawn by fairy music to seek an Otherworld lover. In the tale of Laoghaire, the king frees the wife of an Other-worldly friend.

okr.objective: The record covers tales of heroes lured to the Otherworld.
key_results: A fairy woman lures Connla away.
Cormac is drawn by fairy music.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
